source.text: A purchase above EUR 5,000 must receive Finance approval before the purchase order is issued.
For a purchase of exactly EUR 5,000, Finance approval is not required.
For a purchase below EUR 5,000, the department manager may approve it but is not obliged to do so.
A requester must never approve their own purchase request.
An emergency purchase is exempt from obtaining competitive quotations.
The emergency quotation exemption does not remove the Finance approval requirement above EUR 5,000.
Only the Head of Finance can provide the Finance approval; the buyer cannot provide it.
If a requester cancels a request before approval, that requester must record the cancellation reason.
Approval records must be retained for at least 30 calendar days and cannot be deleted earlier.
The purchase threshold applies separately to each request, not to the monthly total for a supplier.
Different suppliers may have the same supplier name; supplier name is not a unique identifier.
The retention period begins on the approval date, not the purchase-order date.
A new supplier must complete identity verification before its first purchase order.
The Compliance officer performs identity verification; the buyer does not perform it.
For a low-risk supplier, Compliance may request a site visit but is not obliged to request one.
A high-risk supplier must undergo an enhanced review.
A renewal for an existing supplier with no changed identity data is exempt from repeating identity verification.
The renewal exemption does not apply when the supplier changes its legal name.
A buyer must not activate a supplier flagged as blocked.
A risk score of 70 or more is classified as high risk.
Risk scores below 70 are classified as low risk.
Approval expires 365 calendar days after its approval date.
Changing a supplier bank account requires a new independent bank-account check before the next payment.
Two supplier records may share a contact email address; the email address is not unique.
An invoice requires both an existing purchase order and a receipt record before automatic payment.
An invoice variance of exactly EUR 10 is within tolerance.
An invoice variance above EUR 10 blocks automatic payment.
For a blocked invoice, an Accounts Payable analyst may ask for a corrected invoice but is not obliged to ask.
Only the receiving team records goods receipt; Accounts Payable cannot record goods receipt.
The person who changed supplier bank details must not approve payment to those details.
For a service invoice, an authorised service acceptance replaces the goods receipt record.
Service acceptance does not replace the purchase-order requirement.
A dispute freezes the payment clock until the dispute is resolved.
After dispute resolution, the payment clock resumes from its paused value rather than restarting at zero.
An invoice number is unique only within a supplier; different suppliers may reuse the same number.
The tolerance is assessed per invoice, not against the monthly sum of a supplier invoices.
